evidence_basis.originality_note: All learner contexts, wording and numerical values are original. The three complete P2 questions informed derivation and calculation demand only.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prerequisite retrieval, equation recognition, proportional reasoning, general energy change, guided derivation, linked derivation and calculation, then independent two-route synthesis
question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use declared prerequisite knowledge: Q1 directly retrieves work and force relationships, and Q7 mixes those relationships with the new kinetic-energy derivation.

visual_planning.reason: Two later structured questions benefit from original motion-state diagrams. No image assets were created in this four-file task.

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force F acts in the direction of an object's displacement s and gives an object of mass m acceleration a. State the expressions for the work done W and for F in terms of m and a.
Which relationship removes time and connects u, v, a and s in a constant-acceleration derivation of kinetic energy?
An object has kinetic energy E at speed v. Its mass stays fixed and its speed becomes 2v. What is its new kinetic energy?
A constant resultant force changes the speed of an object of mass m from u to v. Which expression equals the work done by the resultant force?

An object of mass m starts from rest. A constant resultant force F acts along displacement s and the object reaches speed v. Starting from W = Fs, derive E_K = 1/2 mv^2. State why the work done can be identified with the final kinetic energy.

A 12 kg laboratory cart speeds up uniformly from 3.0 m s^-1 to 7.0 m s^-1 while a constant resultant force acts along its displacement. Derive an expression for the work done in terms of m, u and v. Then calculate the work done on the cart and interpret the sign of your answer.

figure.purpose: Assess interpretation of initial and final motion states without revealing the derivation
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a laboratory cart at two positions on a horizontal track. Label mass 12 kg, initial speed 3.0 m s^-1 and final speed 7.0 m s^-1. Show one unlabeled rightward resultant-force arrow and displacement s. Include no equations or energy values.
figure.alt_text: A 12 kilogram cart speeds up from 3.0 to 7.0 metres per second along a horizontal track.

questions.prompt: A 6.0 kg trolley moves at 4.0 m s^-1. A constant resultant force of 18 N then acts along the motion through 8.0 m. Use work and kinetic energy to determine the trolley's final speed. Check the result independently using a constant-acceleration equation, and explain why both routes must agree.

figure.purpose: Support a two-route work-energy and motion check
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white diagram of a trolley on a straight track. Label m = 6.0 kg, u = 4.0 m s^-1, F = 18 N and s = 8.0 m. Mark final speed v with a question mark. Do not include formulas or solution steps.
figure.alt_text: A trolley with given mass and initial speed is pushed by a constant force through 8.0 metres toward an unknown final speed.
